title: Let me add my own words to the whisper prompt (Imouto, Gigi Murin, VTuber...)
body:
In a live chat today whisper misheard a few of my own terms: "Imouto" came out as "Immortal", "Gigi Murin" (the Hololive VTuber) as "GG Moon" / "GGMorin", and "VTuber" as "virtual youth table".

The whisper prompt (#667, `whisper-prompt.js`) already biases the decoder toward my name and the names and terms memory picks up. But I have no direct way to add words it should know. The only option is `WHISPER_PROMPT`, which replaces the whole prompt, wake words and name included.

## What I want
- A short list of my own words, e.g. `WHISPER_VOCABULARY=Imouto, Onesan, Gigi Murin, Hololive, VTuber` in `.env`, merged into the built prompt.
- Order: my name first, then my vocabulary, then what memory suggests.
- Stays inside the existing prompt cap (whisper's prompt budget is small), cleaned the same way memory terms are.
- Documented, with those five words as the example.

## Watch out for
Capitalised words in the prompt pull transcription toward them. That's why the "yuzu" in my name-spelling fact is lowercase: "Yuzu" in the prompt made whisper write my name wrong. A vocabulary word that sounds like everyday speech (say "Imouto" and "I'm out to") could start showing up where it shouldn't. Keep the list short and drop a word if that happens.
interface: `buildWhisperPrompt({ facts, userTexts, vocabulary })` takes the vocabulary as an array; `createWhisperPromptProvider({ ..., vocabulary })` takes the raw comma-separated `WHISPER_VOCABULARY` string. The terms go in the existing `Names and terms: ...` part of the prompt.
why: A new env var (WHISPER_VOCABULARY) threaded into whisper-prompt.js. A small feature rather than a bug fix.
